newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco expected to attend W.Sahara talks-diplomat.
newsitem.headline: Morocco expected to attend W.Sahara talks-diplomat.

text.p: Morocco, which for two decades rejected direct talks with the Polisario Front over the disputed Western Sahara, will attend a U.N. sponsored meeting next week at which direct talks are planned, a senior diplomat said on Monday.
The talks are to be held in Lisbon and are expected to last for two days, starting on June 23.
"Morocco will attend the Lisbon meeting...but at this stage the delegation has not been decided," said the diplomat, who asked not to be named.
It was not immediately possible to get confirmation from the Moroccan authorities.
A U.N. spokesman in the Western Saharan town of Laayoun told Reuters on Monday: "As far as we know, Morocco and the Polisario will both attend the Portugal meeting under U.N. auspices."

U.N. special envoy James Baker announced that invitations were being sent to Morocco and the Polisario to attend direct talks, and that Algeria, which backs the Polisario, as well as Mauritania would also be invited.
Baker said last week after indirect talks with the parties in London that "there is some indication that the parties see this as a last best chance to get this (U.N.) plan implemented."
The Polisario and Morocco have been in conflict over the former Spanish territory for around two decades, although a U.N.-sponsored ceasefire has been in effect since September 1991.

It was due to be followed by a referendum in January 1992 to give the people of the territory the choice between independence, as sought by the Polisario, or integration with Morocco which claims the territory.
